subject: Proposal: risk ladder & acceptance for payments promptset A/B rollout
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stripe.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: risk ladder & acceptance for payments promptset A/B rollout

Team — sending a short proposal to land acceptance criteria and a risk ladder for the payments promptset (v3) A/B canary we discussed. Goal is to make the rollout decision objective and to surface clear rollback triggers so support/ops know when to act. Attach: payments_prompt_v3.prompt + metrics_proposal.xlsx.

High level proposal (ask: please review and reply with owners + tweaks by EOD):
- Primary business signals to monitor (A/B variant vs control):
  - Payment auth success rate (per-customer, global)
  - False-positive rate for declined legitimate transactions (fraud FP)
  - Customer-reported declined payments (CS tickets)
  - Latency: model p95 and impact on overall checkout latency
  - Cost delta per 1k requests
- Acceptance thresholds (suggested):
  - Auth success degradation <= 0.2% absolute
  - Fraud FP delta <= +0.5% absolute
  - Model p95 added latency < 150ms (end-to-end impact target)
  - Cost delta < +8%
- Rapid rollback triggers (immediate):
  - Any customer-facing outage (payments failures > 1% in 5m window)
  - Fraud FP increase > +1.5% absolute or sustained increase above +0.8% for 30m
  - Alerting from CS with >10 escalations in 1h
- Gradual mitigation ladder: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 2-4h observation windows and automated metric checks at each step.
- Staging run request: run the promptset against the last 48h of anonymized payments traffic in staging and produce per-segment metrics (region, payment method, new vs returning).

Open questions for ops/engineering:
1) Can we capture trace IDs for declined transactions the model flagged so we can quickly correlate logs?
2) Is there a cheap fallback variant (smaller quantized model) we can route to on degrade?
3) Owners for each metric (who owns auth success, fraud FP, CS signal, latency) — please call out.

I can take point on customer comms with Emily (Stripe) once we have acceptance thresholds ironed out.

Thanks,
Grace
Director, Product - Evaluations
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stripe.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2029 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: risk ladder & acceptance for payments promptset A/B rollout

Thanks Grace — good framing. Quick notes from infra/ops perspective and a couple of suggested tighter guards: 

- Agree with the core signals. I want to add an explicit telemetry requirement: every declined txn that differs between control and variant must include a trace_id header we can pull into Logs/Tracing. If we don't get trace IDs we won't be able to root-cause quickly.
- Proposal to tighten the rapid rollback threshold for fraud FP to +0.6% absolute as an automated rollback trigger (with a secondary manual review window at +0.8% before full rollback). The rationale: payments FP spikes are high-impact for customers; we can be more conservative for initial canary.
- Also request a smoke regression test in staging that runs 100k synthetic transactions across common card types and markets — output to the shared Drive doc.
- I can wire up the telemetry hooks and a Canary monitor in the runtime to auto-throttle if p95 latency exceeds 250ms. Need engineering to confirm KV cache warm-up window and whether we can pre-warm on first batch.

Owners (proposal):
- Auth success / business impact: Marissa Cole
- Fraud FP / label delta: Grace O'Connor
- CS signal / escalations: Mina Haddad (ops) + Marissa
- Latency telemetry / rollout automation: Karthik Iyer

I'll stand up the canary monitor once Karthik confirms the endpoints to scrape. Happy to take the lead on initial comms to Stripe.

– Mina
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stripe.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2029 13:17:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: risk ladder & acceptance for payments promptset A/B rollout

Thanks both — aligning. A few concrete acceptance picks and action items below; I uploaded a short AB plan (ab_plan_v1.md) to the Drive link.

Suggested acceptance for rollout (finalized if no objections by EOD):
- Business/quality: Fraud precision on variant >= 92% and recall drop <= 1.0% relative to control
- User impact: Checkout auth success loss <= 0.15% absolute
- Ops: CS escalations < 5 in the first 8 hours per 100k transactions
- Latency: end-to-end p95 added latency <= 120ms (we can be conservative)
- Cost: cost per 1k requests <= +6%

Action items and owners: 
- Marissa: finalize the AB evaluation slice definitions (new vs returning, BIN ranges, region) + produce customer-impact dashboard
- Grace: own the fraud FP breakpoint logic and post-deploy review (2h window)
- Mina: lead the canary monitor and rollback automation
- Karthik: confirm runtime constraints (cache warm, batch size, fallback model) and commit to feature flag name (payment_prompt_v3_flag).

Escalation path: automated rollback -> ops alert to execs (Grace/Marissa) -> 30-min war room if customer impact observed.

If no objections, I'll mark these thresholds and we can move to staging run tomorrow.

Marissa
Head of Product, Payments Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stripe.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2029 15:05:06 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: risk ladder & acceptance for payments promptset A/B rollout

Looping in engineering constraints and a recommended rollout mechanic. Attach: kf_rollout_playbook.pdf.

Technical notes: 
- KV cache warm-up: we recommend a staged pre-warm phase on canary nodes using sampled prefixes (30m) — otherwise first 10k requests will see latency variance. I'll script a warm-up job.
- Batching and batch size: do the A/B runs in micro-batches (batch_size=16) for the first two windows, then increase to 64 after 25% rollout. This keeps p95 tight and cost predictable.
- Fallback: maintain a smaller quantized model (payment_prompt_v3_q8) that we can route to automatically if p95>300ms for 5m or if auth failure spikes. Routing will be at the request-level via feature flag payment_prompt_v3_flag with variant IDs.
- Telemetry endpoints: I can expose the following metrics: payments.auth_success_{variant}, payments.fraud_fp_{variant}, payments.latency_p95_{variant}, payments.cost_per_1k_{variant}. Add tags: region, payment_method, new_vs_returning.

Open items for product: confirm the exact p95 SLA to wire into the monitor and whether we want to run a second staging sweep with cross-region traffic.

- Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

- Data/residency & logs: we'll need to see a mapping for logs that will include PII redaction and SOC 2 mapping for any identifiable payments metadata. Can you share the SOC 2 / logging mapping doc?
- Timeline: our legal/procurement team wants the proposed canary dates and a short note on rollback SLAs before we sign off (we tend to take 48h internal review).
- Customer comms: we'll coordinate a brief partner-facing note if the rollout has any potential for increased declines; prefer a heads-up template we can use.

If you can share the staging report and acceptance threshold doc (Drive link), I will push to our procurement and legal.

— Emily

Thanks — Mina
